To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we identified 54 mutations in 30 type I patients, including two novel recombinant mutations; 2) we found 13 mutations in 24 type II patients, including one novel point mutation; and 3) we found four mutations in four type III patients.
the most common mutations in the British Isles population are N370S and L444P and that there is a high frequency of the R463C and 55bp deletion mutations.
the most common Gaucher’s mutations in British and Irish patients are N370S (30%), R463C (15%), c1263del and L444P (12% each), and RecNciI and RecTL (10% each).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the mutations in the glucocerbroside gene in British and Irish patients.
the molecular basis of the disease and the identification of the mutations responsible for the phenotypes.
the identification of mutations in Gaucher disease and their correlation with clinical phenotype in a British and Irish population.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the most common mutations in British and Irish Gaucher’s disease patients are: N370S, L444P, R463C, c1263del, RecNciI, and RecTL, and these should be included in a mutation screen of this disease.
54 mutations (90%) in 30 of the 46 unrelated British and Irish Gaucher patients were identified, including 13 novel mutations.
the N370S point mutation is associated with mild disease, the L444P with severe disease, and that the R463C and the c1263del are associated with intermediate disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
46 patients from the British Isles have been genotyped and that 54 mutations (90%) have been identified.
the N370S and L444P mutations are the most frequent mutations in the British and Irish population and the R463C and the c1263del alleles are also present at a relatively high frequency.
the L444P/L44P genotype is associated with neurological disease and the N370S/N370S genotype with mild disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spectrum of Gaucher disease is broad and the genotype-phenotype relationship is complex.
the spectrum of mutations in British and Irish patients is different from that of other populations.

a large number of mutations are found in the Gaucher population, and that a comprehensive mutation screen of the glucocerebosidase gene is required to identify the causative mutations in all patients with Gaucher disease.
